Labels of regions and geoframes

Source: R/labels.R
geoscale_labels.Rd

Display names for the members of a GeoScale. A label belongs to a region at a geoframe and to a named variant – a free name such as "name", "short" or a language code – so a region may carry several names. The table is sparse: a geoframe may label every region, some, or none, and whatever has no label is shown by its code. A row with region = NA names the geoframe itself.

Usage

attach_labels_geoscale(
  x,
  labels,
  variant = NULL,
  default = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

geoscale_labels(x, geoframe = NULL, variant = NULL)

geoscale_label(x, region, geoframe, variant = NULL)

Arguments

x

A GeoScale.

labels

A data.frame with columns geoframe, region, label and optionally variant. The nestedscales names frame and member are accepted for the first two.

variant

For attach_labels_geoscale(): the variant the rows belong to when labels has no variant column (default "label"). For the readers: the variant to return; NULL is every variant in geoscale_labels() and the default one in geoscale_label().

default

Name of the variant used when none is asked for. NULL keeps the current default (initially the first variant attached).

overwrite

Replace a label already present for the same region and variant. FALSE (default) makes that an error.

geoframe

The geoframe: for geoscale_labels() a filter (NULL for all), for geoscale_label() the geoframe the codes are at.

region

Character vector of region codes at geoframe; NA stands for the geoframe itself.

Value

attach_labels_geoscale() the GeoScale; geoscale_labels() a data.frame with columns geoframe, region, variant, label; geoscale_label() a character vector as long as region.

Details

attach_labels_geoscale() adds rows (and may set the default variant), geoscale_labels() returns the table, and geoscale_label() looks names up for a vector of codes, returning the code where there is no label. Subsetting and pruning keep the labels of what remains, and the plots use the default variant.

Examples

gs <- attach_labels_geoscale(
  geoscale_example(),
  data.frame(geoframe = "country", region = c("N", "S"),
             label = c("Northland", "Southland")),
  variant = "name"
)
gs <- attach_labels_geoscale(
  gs,
  data.frame(geoframe = "country", region = "N", label = "Nordland"),
  variant = "de"
)
geoscale_labels(gs)
#>   geoframe region variant     label
#> 1  country      N    name Northland
#> 2  country      S    name Southland
#> 3  country      N      de  Nordland
geoscale_label(gs, c("N", "S"), "country")
#> [1] "Northland" "Southland"
geoscale_label(gs, c("N", "S"), "country", variant = "de")
#> [1] "Nordland" "S"       
geoscale_label(gs, c("N1", "ZB"), "zone")     # no labels: the codes
#> [1] "N1" "ZB"
